Among the many Apple Intelligence features coming to iOS 27, the Passwords app is set to gain a particularly powerful capability: automatically changing your passwords for you.

The Passwords app in iOS 27, powered by Apple Intelligence, can handle compromised login accounts on your behalf.

The next generation of Apple Intelligence is at the heart of the upcoming iOS 27 and related software updates. One of the powerful new AI features is related to Apple's Passwords app.

Launched two years ago, the Passwords app serves as a dedicated management centre for login credentials, two-factor authentication codes, Wi-Fi passwords, passkeys, and more.

The app has always alerted you to issues with passwords in your database. For example, if your password has appeared in a data breach or is reused across multiple accounts, the Passwords app will notify you.

However, until now, you still had to handle these problematic login accounts manually yourself.

But Apple says that in iOS 27, in many cases, a newly added agentic AI feature can change your passwords on your behalf. According to its website:

With this feature, you can keep your login accounts secure at all times and use strong passwords, without spending too much effort or time.

iOS 27 is currently in beta testing, and is expected to roll out to all users in a few weeks. The new Passwords feature is expected to debut in iOS 27.0, though availability in the beta has been unstable, so it may be delayed and officially arrive in iOS 27.1.

Have you tried the new Passwords feature in iOS 27 beta? How was your experience? Feel free to share in the comments.
